narr: A weak frontal boundary and associated surface low pressure remained stationary across North-central Louisiana on August 24th. Precipitable water values were on the order of two inches along and south of this boundary. Meanwhile, a weak shortwave trough began to shift southeastward from the Plains into the Four State Region, which served to reinforce the lift along the frontal boundary and resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms in the early morning hours. Widespread rainfall amounts of 3-4 inches with isolated higher amounts in excess of 6 inches fell across parts of La Salle Parish which resulted in multiple reports of flash flooding.
ev: West Elm Street was flooded in Jena.
A portion of Ebenezer Tap Road south of Highway 500 was washed out and closed to traffic.
Taylor Chapel Road and Zeagler Cutoff Road were both flooded in the Summerville community.
